graded_map.identification: The elementary-symmetric theorem identifies R_N with S_N^{(𝔖_N)^r}; ι_N is injective and preserves the displayed weights, with 𝔖_N the symmetric group on N letters.

factor_maps.specialization: For J=(j_1,…,j_r)∈{1,…,N}^r, σ_J:K[U_1,…,U_r]→S_N sends every U_a↦T_(j_a)^(a).
factor_maps.source_factorization: The ath input coordinate factors as ∏_(l=1)^N(1+T_l^(a)t). The maps of1.7 are Z-multilinear, that is, group homomorphisms in each argument separately. Expanding successively in all r arguments therefore yields one image factor for each tuple J=(j_1,…,j_r).
factor_maps.image_identification: Naturality and the iterated separate group-homomorphism identities give Φ(∏_l(1+T_l^(1)t),…,∏_l(1+T_l^(r)t))=∏_Jσ_J(θ) in the multiplicative series examples, and the corresponding Σ_Jσ_J(θ) in the additive series example.

weight_calculation: The source stipulates that every isobaric component of the coefficient of t^q in θ has weight between q and mq. Every σ_J sends each degree-one U_a to a degree-one root variable, preserving the monomial weights.

A contribution to the coefficient of t^d in the product has indices q_J≥0 with Σ_Jq_J=d. The coefficient at q=0 is the multiplicative identity. Each surviving monomial has weight W=Σ_Jw_J, hence d=Σ_Jq_J≤W≤Σ_Jm q_J=md.
For the additive target, each summand in degree d has its original weight between d and md, so the same bounds hold.

The resulting coefficient is separately symmetric in each root family. The injective graded elementary-symmetric map descends it to the universal polynomial without altering its weights. The filtration passage used in1.6 fixes each finite coefficient and hence these bounds.

At the coefficient index printed k in the final clause, the endpoint is m·k=km. The preceding isolated baseline dot is surplus punctuation before this product; the calculation introduces no additional scalar or operation.
decision: Preserve the observed leading dot in the diplomatic layer; keep the corrected endpoint km. No replacement mathematical claim is introduced.
